chapter: Los Angeles scene and the Ellington sound
title: The Ambassador and Coconut Grove
summary: Gus Arnheim and others played the hotel, and Brown never frequented it, spending his Los Angeles visits with family.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You mentioned the Ambassador Hotel. That was -- did that have the Coconut Grove operating?
Who played the Coconut Grove? What kind of acts were in there?
Oh, they had a nice big band.
Who was the band at the Coconut Grove? At the Ambassador Hotel?

Well, they changed from time to time, and I remember Gus Arnheim and oh, many different bands that played these hotels and spots around town, Cinderella Roof, and oh, lots of places, too numerous to mention, because there were -- that was way back.
Freddie Martin was there that early, wasn't he?
He was -- I think the Ambassador, I think he was a little later than some of these others. Freddie
hasn't been out too long, I don't believe. I wouldn't say Freddie's been out over eight years, or more. I really don't know right now.
Did places like the Coconut Grove and the Ambassador Hotel have just big bands, or did they have other acts too? They had dancers --
-- shows, like a show, a floor shows, and --
Can you name any of the people that appeared there then?

No, because I never went down that way. I -- the first time I went in the Coconut Grove was to a dance that we played, and later on to some private parties, but I never -- never got there, because I came out here every year and went around while I was out here, but mostly I hung out with the family, so I didn't do much cabaretting or sight-seeing.
When you say that "we played" do you mean Duke's band?
Ellington's band, yes. We played the --
No, I don't even remember that.
